title: Naa20 perturbation lowers Cyp46a1 and partially induces sterol-biosynthesis transcripts in inhibitory and hypothalamic neurons
exact_observed_result: Naa20 perturbation repeatedly repressed Cyp46a1, including 151 TH logFC -0.3913479745388031 FDR 1.2864940556785837e-13, 155 MB logFC -0.7657643556594849 FDR 1.028870838384272e-10, and 191 MB P MY GABA logFC -1.036651372909546 FDR 2.548633596417313e-06. Sterol biosynthesis genes were induced in subsets, including Cyp51 and Mvk in 145 MH-LH TH Glut and Fdft1, Sc5d, and Srebf2 in 191 MB P MY GABA.
biological_interpretation: NatB/Naa20 perturbation couples repression of the brain cholesterol-turnover enzyme Cyp46a1 to a partial compensatory sterol-synthesis response in selected inhibitory, midbrain, and thalamic/hypothalamic neurons.

title: Matr3 lowering induces a specific RBP liability program led by Atp9b, Ddhd1, E2f4, Zkscan3, and Rsrp1
exact_observed_result: Matr3 lowering induced a recurrent Atp9b/Ddhd1/E2f4/Zkscan3/Kcnq2/Sugp2/Uggt2-up and Rsrp1-down core across 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA; Fus and Tardbp were active comparators but did not reproduce that MATR3 core.

title: AP-2 subunit loss converges on a Tfrc-positive, sterol-repressed endocytosis state
exact_observed_result: Ap2m1 and Ap2s1 loss converged on AP-2 dysfunction in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, including FDR-supported Tfrc induction under both perturbations and shared repression of Prkcb/Mical2/Kcnn3-like output genes; Ap2s1 also produced a 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut activity/neurotrophin branch with Egr3, Arc, and Vgf repression, and both AP-2 subunits lowered sterol genes in 155 MB Glut.
biological_interpretation: The response is consistent with loss of the AP-2 clathrin adaptor rather than a generic endocytic perturbation: AP2M1 and AP2S1 encode physical AP-2 subunits, transferrin-receptor uptake is known to be AP-2-dependent, and the neuronal mRNA response couples a putative TFRC compensation axis to cell-type-restricted sterol and excitability outputs.

title: Zbtb11 loss represses a mitochondrial, nucleolar, endomembrane, and glycan program in vulnerable subcortical neurons
exact_observed_result: Zbtb11 perturbation produced 48 FDR genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 17 in 191 MB P MY GABA, and 16 in 155 MB Glut. The recurrent core was down-regulated and included Rbm28, Taf1b, Stx16, Pigq, Man2c1, Gtpbp3, Acsf3, Ndufc2, Ndufaf1, and Ttc4, with 151 TH examples such as Rbm28 logFC -1.460 FDR 3.57e-16 and Acsf3 logFC -1.146 FDR 7.68e-09.
biological_interpretation: Zbtb11 loss selectively suppresses a mixed mitochondrial, RNA polymerase I/nucleolar, endomembrane, GPI-biosynthesis, and glycan-catabolic abundance program, matching known ZBTB11 mitochondrial and neurodevelopmental disease biology but showing that the response is not shared by arbitrary ZBTB-family perturbations.

title: Pura loss produces a robust thalamic and midbrain Igip/Nefl remodeling program
exact_observed_result: Pura was FDR-depleted only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, the two classes with multi-gene corrected programs. Both shared Igip down, Ogt down and Nefl up; 151 TH additionally induced Cntnap1, Kcna6, Lingo1 and Tubb2a and lowered Fbxo33 and Setd7, whereas 155 MB included Pcsk1n down and Nlgn2/Ubqln2/Dgkz up.
biological_interpretation: PUR-alpha loss acutely remodels a structural and neurofilament-like RNA state in specific glutamatergic neurons, with Igip as a recurrent downregulated neighboring transcript that could reflect either PURA biology or local cis-locus effects.

title: Wdr26 loss exposes caudal and subcortical neuronal CTLH-liability signatures that Gnb1 does not explain
exact_observed_result: The raw footprint proposal was verified against the Wdr26 report: FDR<0.05 burdens were 1459 genes in 308 CB GABA, 491 in 155 MB Glut, 329 in 191 MB P MY GABA, 43 in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 13 in 151 TH, with 16/21 groups FDR-silent. Exact rows included Srrm2, Luc7l2, Kpna1, Cacna1g, and Grik1 down in 308 CB GABA; Srrm2, Nat8l, and Atp1b1 down plus Dync1h1 up in 155 MB Glut; and Col11a2 up with Srrm2, Atp1a3, and Kcna2 down in 191 MB P MY GABA. Gnb1 depletion was efficient in overlapping classes but nearly orthogonal to Wdr26.
biological_interpretation: Wdr26 perturbation exposes a posterior and subcortical neuronal RNA-processing/excitability state linked to the WDR26-CTLH disease gene, not a simple consequence of depleting the assayed G-protein beta subunit.

title: Nipbl, Smc1a, and Stag2 converge on a thalamic cohesin-loader neuronal projection program
exact_observed_result: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Nipbl, Smc1a, and Stag2 perturbations shared down-regulation of Ptprm, Necab2, Smtn, and Adamts2 and Stag2-neighbor correlations prioritized Smc1a, Smc3, and Nipbl, whereas Stag1, Pds5a, and Hdac8 did not fully phenocopy the state.
biological_interpretation: A subset of cohesin-loader and ring perturbations exposes a thalamic projection/synapse vulnerability distinct from simple pan-cohesin or Cornelia-de-Lange-gene interchangeability.

title: Ranbp2 knockdown yields gated RNA/SUMO and calcium-synaptic programs rather than a uniform nuclear-pore response
exact_observed_result: Ranbp2 knockdown produced FDR-positive signatures in 6 of 20 tested cell types. 022 L5 ET CTX Glut had FDR-supported target depletion, Ranbp2 logFC -0.536 and FDR 0.00653, plus a 56-gene mixed RNA/nuclear response including Gpr162, Dync1h1, Rbm15, Kmt2a, Srrm2, and Pcbp1. 308 CB GABA instead had 98 FDR genes enriched for calcium/synaptic transcripts, including Grm1, Epha4, Itpr1, Prkcg, Kcna6, Dlg2, and Cacna2d2.
biological_interpretation: A RANBP2/SUMO nuclear-pore perturbation is read out differently by different neurons: cortical L5 ET cells couple it to RNA and nuclear-protein abundance, whereas cerebellar GABA cells expose a calcium/synaptic program.

title: ELP1 and BDP1 reductions activate an ATF4 amino-acid-starvation module in susceptible thalamic neurons
exact_observed_result: Elp1 induced an ATF4-like amino-acid-starvation panel across susceptible neurons, Bdp1 induced a concordant 151 TH Ddit3/aminoacyl-tRNA-synthetase state, and Trmt1 did not induce the same Elp1/Elp2 ISR-like module in 151 TH.
biological_interpretation: Elongator loss and Pol III initiation stress sensitize a thalamic tRNA/translation pathway that is not a generic consequence of every tRNA-modification perturbation.

title: Proteasome subunit loss couples proteasome compensation to neuronal-state repression
exact_observed_result: Psmb4, Psmc1, Psmc5, and Pomp perturbations produced overlapping neuronal proteasome-stress states: responsive classes up-regulated proteasome and proteostasis genes such as Psme4, Psmc6, Psmd4, and Nfe2l1-linked targets while repeatedly repressing synaptic and excitability genes including Atp1a3, Gria2, and related neuronal-state transcripts.
biological_interpretation: Direct loss of proteasome core, 19S ATPase, or maturation activity is not a benign compensatory proteasome upshift; in vulnerable neurons it pairs proteasome recovery signatures with loss of ion-channel, receptor, and mature neuronal expression.
cell_types: ["052 Pvalb Gaba", "066 CNU-HYa HY GABA", "110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut", "155 MB Glut", "191 MB P MY GABA", "001 L5-6 IT Glut", "005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut", "151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut", "054 CNU-MGE GABA"]
caveats: ["Pomp, Psmc1, and Psmc5 target-transcript depletion was often not FDR-confirmed, so downstream signatures should not be scaled as mRNA knockdown dose responses.", "This is a broad proteasome-stress axis and should not be used to nominate a single safe proteasome subunit to inhibit."]
prior_expectation: Core proteasome and assembly perturbations are expected to activate NFE2L1/Nrf1-mediated proteasome recovery; the neuronal loss of synaptic and ion-homeostasis transcripts adds a cell-state liability arm.
power_assessment: Several proteasome nodes show positive convergence in 155 and lower-yield inhibitory contexts; self-transcript FDR is not used as an engagement gate.
adjudication_reason: Proteasome recovery coupled to mature-neuronal repression defines a consequential liability state rather than benign feedback alone.

title: Grin2a and Grin2b oppose an L2/3 cortical Nptx2-Bdnf-Ptgs2 program
exact_observed_result: Grin2a perturbation raised Nptx2, Bdnf, Ptgs2, and Cckbr in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut and Nptx2 in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut; in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, Grin2b perturbation was FDR-supported for Grin2b and Kcnv1 and drove the same Nptx2/Bdnf/Ptgs2/Vgf/Cckbr markers in the opposite direction at nominal-to-FDR levels. 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut buffered strong Grin2a depletion.
biological_interpretation: NR2A and NR2B loss are not interchangeable in upper-layer cortical excitatory neurons; the direction of chronic subunit depletion depends on cortical subtype and NMDAR subunit identity.
cell_types: ["005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut", "007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut", "151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut"]
caveats: ["Several Grin2b opposite-direction marker rows in L2/3 were nominal rather than FDR-significant, although Vgf and Kcnv1 passed FDR.", "Grin2a mRNA itself was strongly FDR-depleted in 151 TH but did not induce Nptx2, Bdnf, or Ptgs2 there."]
prior_expectation: GRIN2A and GRIN2B encode distinct NMDA receptor GluN2 subunits with established synaptic signaling roles; the observed opposite chronic RNA outputs refine rather than simply mirror generic NMDAR activation literature.
power_assessment: Opposite GRIN2A/GRIN2B marker directions are positively observed in cortical 005/007; 151 silence is not used as a functional matched-null control.
adjudication_reason: Opposite chronic GluN2A/GluN2B cortical outputs could materially revise subunit-specific plasticity models, but nominal tail genes prevent stronger Support.

title: Eef2 loss induces a cortical L2/3 Vgf/Cx3cl1/Son/Ranbp2/Smpd1 state rather than a generic elongation signature
exact_observed_result: Eef2 perturbation produced its largest FDR signature in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut with 575 genes, including Vgf logFC 2.149 and FDR 1.01e-08, Nptx2 logFC 2.946 and FDR 3.02e-08, Cx3cl1 logFC 0.864 and FDR 4.93e-08, and Uchl1 logFC -0.712 and FDR 5.35e-05. biological_interpretation: The mRNA response to Eef2 perturbation is strongly state-gated and biased toward superficial cortical excitatory neurons instead of reading out simple pan-neuronal translation elongation failure.

title: Braf/Map2k1/Shoc2, but not Raf1 or Mapk1, gate the TH Vgf/Ptpn5/Etv5 MAPK output
exact_observed_result: The 151 TH Vgf/Ptpn5/Etv5 MAPK module was repressed by Braf and Map2k1 loss and induced by Nf1 loss; Shoc2 was preferentially Braf/Map2k1-like, whereas Raf1, Map2k2, Mapk1, Ptpn1, and Rasa2 failed to reproduce the module. / In 151 TH Prkcd/Grin2c Glut, Map2k1 and Braf loss repressed a focused Vgf/Ptpn5/Unc13a/Etv5 program, Nf1 loss moved the axis oppositely, and Map2k2 did not reproduce the MEK1-sensitive module. / In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, a nominal Lztr1 module was concordant with Nf1 loss and opposed to Braf, Kras, Map2k1, and Shoc2 loss, giving weak Lztr1 downstream DE a directionally interpretable RAS/MAPK readout. / Nf1 perturbation induced Egr1, Etv4, Etv5, Dusp4, Dusp6, Spry4, Ptpn5, Unc13a, Scg2, Tnfrsf12a, and Vgf most strongly in thalamic and midbrain subclasses; Cic loss shared only a subset of these MAPK-responsive genes in the same thalamic hotspot. / Braf, Map2k1, and Mapk1 loss-of-function signatures opposed Nf1 on Nf1-responsive genes in 151 TH, 155 MB, and 191 MB P MY GABA, consistent with NF1 loss derepressing Ras while RAF/MEK/ERK loss reduces pathway flux. Parquet-verified leading rows: Cic->Lrrc7 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut log2FC -0.39, FDR 1.24e-16; Nf1->Vgf in 155 MB Glut log2FC 2.19, FDR 1.75e-16; Nf1->Vgf in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut log2FC 0.848, FDR 1.36e-11; Cic->Spock3 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut log2FC -0.395, FDR 6.01e-10; Cic->Atp2a2 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut log2FC -0.274, FDR 1.35e-09; Nf1->Vgf in 191 MB P MY GABA log2FC 1.87, FDR 1.78e-09.
biological_interpretation: Resting neuronal MAPK output is branch-specific, with SHOC2 feeding a BRAF/MEK1-like Vgf/Ptpn5/Etv5 state and ERK2 transcript knockdown buffered or bypassed at the mRNA endpoint. / A directional RAF-MEK transcriptional readout is strongest at MEK1/BRAF/NF1 in thalamic glutamatergic neurons and is not a generic RAS-family or MEK-paralog null. / LZTR1 may act in the same thalamic RAS/MAPK polarity space as NF1 and RAF/MEK nodes, but the observed Lztr1 response remains weak. / NF1 loss derepresses a subtype-biased Ras/MAPK feedback state in mature neurons, with CIC overlapping only partially rather than serving as a full NF1 proxy. / The atlas recovers the expected polarity of Ras/MAPK regulation at the transcriptome level in selected neuronal classes, while wild-type Hras loss is not a proxy for activated-HRAS or NF1-loss states.

title: SIN3A loss drives a cilium/centrosome and cholesterol/Grn response with spliceosome repression that is distinct from REST and generic HDAC-associated chromatin loss
exact_observed_result: Sin3a targeting produced a cell-type-skewed FDR chromatin-regulator phenotype with recurrent cilium/centrosome and Cyp46a1/Grn induction plus spliceosome and RNA-processing repression; in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Phf21a and Sin3a had opposite Rreb1 directions, Rest failed to derepress classic NRSE targets, and a second comparison found a weak Max-positive Sin3a component distinct from Myc/Mycn, Mecp2, Chd4, Gatad2b, Mbd2, and HDAC perturbations. biological_interpretation: SIN3A scaffold loss has a specific neuronal output that is not a generic REST, NuRD, HDAC, or MYC-family phenocopy despite shared repressor-complex annotations.

title: MEF2C and MEF2A expose paralog-specific cortical and thalamic programs
exact_observed_result: Mef2c perturbation drove a cortical IT synaptic/membrane program in 005 L4-5 and 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, while Mef2a’s FDR-supported downstream response was restricted to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut with Gpr4, Ogt, Prkcg, and Sez6. No assayed perturbation was a strong Mef2c-like or anti-Mef2c neighbor in the two high-signal cortical classes.

title: Srrm2 depletion is tolerated in several cortical classes but drives abundance programs in thalamic, midbrain, and related GABAergic neurons
exact_observed_result: Acute Srrm2 depletion produced a highly cell-state-selective abundance phenotype in which thalamic, midbrain, and related GABAergic classes carried most corrected downstream responses, while several cortical and Pvalb classes reduced Srrm2 without corrected off-target genes. / Multiple FDR-supported perturbations in RNA-processing factors or Huwe1 produced nonuniform neuronal signatures centered on Srrm2, Srsf-family, Rsrp1, Tcea2, Pabpn1, and related spliceosome or nuclear-speckle transcripts, with thalamic and midbrain classes repeatedly carrying the broadest response while other target-shifted classes were buffered.
biological_interpretation: The nuclear-speckle factor SRRM2 is a loss-of-function vulnerability for a subset of thalamic/midbrain neuronal states rather than a universal neuronal transcript-abundance dependency. / Selected subcortical neurons are acutely sensitive to partial nuclear-speckle or spliceosome stress, so local SR-factor/nuclear-speckle marker panels should be better pharmacodynamic and liability readouts than the target-RNA row alone.

title: Obligate NMDAR Grin1 loss produces a thalamic Scg2/Stmn4/Kctd16/Gpm6a program not shared by Grin2d
exact_observed_result: Grin1 was strongly depleted in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and produced 89 FDR<0.05 genes there. The same contrast induced Scg2, Stmn4, Kctd16, Gpm6a, Igf1, and Jun while reducing Erc2, Homer2, Kcnab2, Gabrd, and Prkcd. Grin2a, Grin2b, Dlg4, Grid1, Grik5, Camk2b, Nrxn1, and Shank3 were target-depleted in 151 TH, but only Grin1 produced a broad 151 TH response.
biological_interpretation: Loss of the obligate GluN1 subunit creates a thalamic synaptic/growth-factor state that is not reproduced by depleting individual modulatory NMDAR subunits or postsynaptic scaffolds.

title: Zc3h14 loss links thalamic and midbrain glutamatergic responses to Pabpn1/Cstf2 repression and Zcchc18 induction
exact_observed_result: Zc3h14 loss produced six FDR rows in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, including Zcchc18 logFC 0.515 FDR 7.98e-10, Pabpn1 -0.264 FDR 9.51e-04, and Tra2a 0.427 FDR 0.00402. 155 MB Glut had clearer Zc3h14 target depletion, logFC -0.739 FDR 0.00543, plus Zcchc18 induction, Pabpn1 repression, and Cstf2 repression. 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA and 191 MB P MY GABA gave narrower single-gene FDR responses.
biological_interpretation: Zc3h14 knockdown connects a conserved poly(A)-binding protein to a selective neuronal RNA-processing abundance state, with Pabpn1/Cstf2 down-regulation in glutamatergic responders and Zcchc18 as the most reproducible positive marker.

title: Qrich1 perturbation lowers a Scn2b/Celf3/Ldhd/Tlcd3b module in thalamic and brainstem/midbrain neurons
exact_observed_result: Qrich1 perturbation yielded 75 FDR genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, led by Scn2b logFC -1.277 FDR 6.86e-37, Celf3 -1.353 FDR 1.24e-30, Ldhd -1.981 FDR 3.67e-22, and Map1a -0.686 FDR 2.58e-08. 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA reproduced the Celf3/Ldhd/Tlcd3b or Celf3/Map1a/Ldhd down-regulated core at smaller breadth.
biological_interpretation: A broadly expressed nucleoplasmic QRICH1 target produces a sharply biased neuronal expression module centered on thalamic and caudal populations, with recurrent repression of ion-channel, RNA-binding, and metabolic genes rather than a uniform brain-wide knockdown state.

title: Marchf6 and Txndc15 losses induce a narrow neuronal SREBP2 sterol module
exact_observed_result: Marchf6 loss induced Insig1, Dhcr24, Cyp51, Msmo1, Hmgcr, Fdft1, Hmgcs1, Ldlr, Fdps, Sqle, and Srebf2 in 151 TH and 155 MB, while Txndc15 loss induced Hmgcs1, Insig1, Ldlr, Srebf2, Fdft1, and Dhcr24 in 155 MB and a weaker Insig1-led 191 MB P MY GABA sterol response; Amfr showed only nominal opposite sterol skew.

title: Xpo1 gain in caudal neurons induces Arrdc3/Slc16a6/Vamp2/Sun2 and represses RNA-processing transcripts without mimicking selinexor-like inhibition
exact_observed_result: Xpo1 targeting increased Xpo1 RNA in the strongest responsive classes and produced a bidirectional module: Arrdc3, Slc16a6, Vamp2, and Sun2 rose while Snrnp70, Arglu1, Pabpn1, and Srsf-family rows fell. biological_interpretation: This is an Xpo1-transcript gain state coupled to RNA-processing repression and is directionally distinct from pharmacologic CRM1/XPO1 inhibition by selinexor.

title: Gfpt1/HBP suppression induces a selective ER and integrated-stress program with recurrent Ogt repression

title: Bmal1, Clock, and Rev-erb perturbations converge on a 151 TH clock-output and synaptic branch
exact_observed_result: Bmal1 and Clock perturbations lowered core clock outputs such as Dbp and Nr1d2 in responsive thalamic/midbrain classes; Nr1d1 perturbation induced Npas2, Cry2, Dbp, Ciart, and Nfil3 plus neuronal genes in 151 TH; and Nr1d2 loss recurrently induced Nr1d1 with weak reciprocal Nr1d1-to-Nr1d2 compensation.
biological_interpretation: The 151 TH circadian feedback loop is recoverable by CRISPRi but asymmetric: BMAL1/CLOCK and REV-ERB perturbations share part of the branch while CRY1, CRY2, and ROR-family perturbations split by marker and polarity.

title: Hspa8 depletion induces compensatory HSP70/HSP90 folding feedback in selected neurons
exact_observed_result: Hspa8 perturbation induced a chaperone arm in several classes. 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut contained nine FDR genes, including Dnaja1 logFC 0.496 FDR 0.000723, Hspa4l 0.394 FDR 0.000723, Hsp90aa1 0.383 FDR 0.00252, and Cct6a 0.700 FDR 0.0203. Hsp90aa1 was also induced in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and positive nominal calls recurred for Hsph1, Dnaja1, Dnajb1, Hsp90aa1, Stip1, and Hspa4l across the 21 tested classes.
biological_interpretation: Loss of the constitutive HSP70-family chaperone Hspa8 releases a compensatory folding program rather than an isolated hit list, and the closest recurrent neighbors were proteasome perturbations rather than most annotated chaperones.

title: Ppp3ca and Ppp3r1 loss expose a noncanonical thalamic calcineurin module
exact_observed_result: Ppp3ca and Ppp3r1 were both FDR-depleted in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and produced compact but nonidentical calcineurin-subunit signatures. Ppp3ca increased Pcsk1n, Ptpn3, Iyd and Pik3r1, whereas Ppp3r1 increased Pcsk1n/Ptprs and lowered Atp2a2, Coro6, Slc6a17, Tle2 and Ndrg2; AP-2 adaptor perturbations were the strongest anticorrelated Ppp3r1 neighbors in this same signature space.
biological_interpretation: Calcineurin-subunit loss in thalamic neurons is captured by a small synaptic/calcium and endocytic-countermodule rather than by an NFAT/RCAN transcript reporter.

title: Actb loss recurrently induces Actg1 and Flna compensation in selected neuronal classes
exact_observed_result: Actb perturbation recurrently induced Actg1 and Flna, with a 9-gene all-up signature in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and a 5-gene all-up signature in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut; Actg1 perturbation did not reciprocally produce a broad Actb-like state and had only Flna as a non-self FDR hit in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut.
biological_interpretation: Beta-actin loss elicits asymmetric gamma-actin and Filamin-A compensation plus selected adhesion/actomyosin remodeling, fitting prior evidence that cytoplasmic actin isoforms are closely related but nonredundant.

title: SRSF1 loss rewires a recurrent splice-regulator network instead of inducing SRSF2 compensation

title: Tcf7l2 aligns with Ctnnb1 and opposes Apc at the beta-catenin/TCF node in 151 TH neurons
exact_observed_result: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Apc perturbation induced Wnt feedback genes Axin2, Nkd1, and Notum and repressed neuronal markers such as Grin2c, Gls, Cck, and Chgb; Ctnnb1 knockdown produced a large response with the opposite beta-catenin/TCF direction for many targets, while Tcf7l2 overlapped only part of the Apc signature and changed Cck and Spock3 in the direction opposite to Apc.
biological_interpretation: The signatures place Apc, Ctnnb1, and Tcf7l2 at the Wnt/beta-catenin/TCF node in a thalamic neuronal context, but the neuronal outputs include synaptic and subtype markers rather than only canonical Axin2/Nkd1 feedback.

title: Pten loss aligns with Tsc1/Tsc2 loss and opposes Mtor/Pik3ca while remodeling Akt3 and Pik3r1 transcripts
exact_observed_result: Pten perturbation produced FDR-supported thalamic and midbrain responses marked by Ypel3, Pcsk1n, and Pink1 repression with Epha10 and Haghl induction, and its restricted signature aligned with Tsc1/Tsc2 while opposing Mtor/Rptor/Pik3ca. The related Depdc5 and Tsc1/Tsc2 perturbations induced a 151 TH sterol arm, whereas Mtor and Rptor were much subtler direct negative comparators.
biological_interpretation: The atlas recovers the expected PI3K-AKT-TSC-mTOR polarity as a transcriptomic epistasis pattern: upstream inhibitory lesions such as Pten, Tsc1/Tsc2, and Depdc5 point toward an mTORC1-like state and Mtor/Rptor depletion points against it. The readout is distal RNA remodeling rather than a direct measurement of PIP3, phospho-AKT, or phospho-S6.

title: MYEF2 perturbation repeatedly induces a compact Dzip3/Vbp1/Ist1 module in posterior neuronal classes
exact_observed_result: Myef2 ranked first among all perturbations by the mean score of Dzip3, Vbp1, and Ist1 in seven posterior or subcortical cell types. biological_interpretation: The response is a compact and unusually specific Myef2 RNA marker module, although existing prior literature links MYEF2 to transcriptional repression rather than to a known DZIP3/VBP1/IST1 pathway.

title: Phf12 converges with Gatad1 while KDM5, SIN3A, and GATAD2B do not
exact_observed_result: In informative Gatad1-responsive glutamatergic populations, Phf12 converged with the Gatad1 signature, while Kdm5b, Kdm5c, Sin3a, and Gatad2b were near-zero or divergent; Gatad1 also induced Phf12 and nominally Kdm5a. / Phf12 induced a strong mixed Ptcd3/Chpf2/Atp6v0b/Stx16/Sf3b2/Stk16 module and repressed Gls, Grin2c, Snap25, and Tubb3, while Kmt2e and Gatad1 also produced narrow 151/155 responses with recurrent Atp6v0b, Chpf2, Ptcd3, Sfswap, Vps50, Snhg11, or Eno2 induction.
biological_interpretation: GATAD1 loss is tied to a selective PHF12-linked chromatin neighborhood rather than to generic KDM5, SIN3A, or NuRD subunit perturbation. / A subset of posterior glutamatergic neurons routes perturbations of PHF12/KMT2E/GATAD1 chromatin machinery into an organellar and RNA-processing response coupled to loss of synaptic transcripts.

title: Atrx and Chd8 perturbations move Csf2ra in opposite directions in TH and MB glutamatergic neurons
exact_observed_result: Atrx produced only ten FDR<0.05 rows across 18 tested cell types, but Csf2ra was FDR-repressed in both 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut. Chd8 induced Csf2ra in those same cell classes with FDR support.
biological_interpretation: The Csf2ra marker is not a generic chromatin-loss response: ATRX and CHD8 have opposite signed effects on the same transcript in the two strongest Csf2ra-responsive neuronal contexts.

title: NatB and NatA perturbations produce separable posterior neuronal signatures
exact_observed_result: Naa20 perturbation lowered a recurrent Snhg11/Kifc2/Repin1/Atp11b branch across thalamic, midbrain and selected GABAergic neurons without FDR-significant Naa20 mRNA depletion. Naa15 produced a different posterior NatA state with Ldhd, Actr1b, Matk, Ring1 and Idh3g induction and Rtn3/Thy1/Atp1b1 repression, while Naa10 remained under-engaged and did not phenocopy either program.
biological_interpretation: Partial NatB and NatA disruption have separable neuronal consequences, so loss of one N-terminal acetyltransferase subunit cannot be inferred from the other; recurrent downstream modules are better engagement readouts than Naa20 transcript abundance.

title: USP48 depletion selectively induces a thalamic ABHD12B/RESP18 endomembrane signature
exact_observed_result: Usp48 perturbation had its best self-RNA decrease in 151 TH and generated exactly 10 FDR genes there: Abhd12b, Resp18, Galk2, Msrb2, Tmem181a, Syne1, Bcan, Lrp10 and Macf1 up, with Cyp46a1 down; all non-151 Usp48 contrasts had zero FDR genes.
biological_interpretation: USP48 loss exposes a compact thalamic neuronal RNA output separable from Usp9x/Uchl1 loss, ARL3 or GSDME substrate biology, and canonical NF-kappaB transcription.

title: Ski loss exposes a narrow L2/3 intratelencephalic cortical marker program instead of a broad TGF-beta/SMAD response
exact_observed_result: Partial Ski perturbation yielded a mixed, FDR-supported neuronal RNA phenotype dominated by L2/3 IT CTX Glut markers including Wscd2, Chd3, Rfx3, Pde4a, Plk5, Ttyh3, and Acsl3, whereas Tgif1, Smad2, and receptor-level TGF-beta perturbations did not recapitulate a canonical SMAD module. title: Hnrnph2 loss couples Rsrp1 repression to TCA-gene induction in thalamic glutamatergic neurons
exact_observed_result: Hnrnph2 perturbation generated only six FDR<0.05 rows across 22 cell types. In 151 TH Prkcd/Grin2c, Hnrnph2 and Rsrp1 were repressed while Idh3g and Ogdh were induced; Hnrnph1, Hnrnpf, Hnrnph3, and Grsf1 had FDR=1.0 in all 88 measured rows.

title: Gtf2i and Gtf2ird1 expose distinct TH Prkcd/Grin2c programs within the Williams-Beuren interval
exact_observed_result: Gtf2i knockdown produced a compact mostly induced 151 TH program with Pnpla6, Plppr3, Rasgrp2, and Kcnk4, while Gtf2ird1 elicited a sparse but different thalamic response with F11r, Sparcl1, Rab30, and Abca3; neither was interchangeable with Baz1b, Fzd9, Limk1, or Clip2.
biological_interpretation: Williams-Beuren critical-region transcription factors are dosage-sensitive in the same thalamic subclass but produce gene-specific rather than locus-general transcriptomic states.

title: Dhx9 and nuclear-pore transport perturbations expose a nuclear RNP/splicing state rather than Dicer/Ago or generic karyopherin loss
exact_observed_result: Dhx9 elicited a cell-selective RNA-processing state involving Trappc11, Glo1, Iqgap1, Prpf38a, Riok3, Atat1, Dusp11, Son, Ccdc93, and Snhg11; Tpr, Tnpo3, and Ranbp2 placed this response near nuclear-pore basket, SR/splicing, and nuclear-transport perturbations but away from Nup93, Kpna3, Xpo7, Dicer/Ago, and Adar arms. / Tpr ranked fourth in the footprint sweep with 5087 significant cell-gene pairs across 10 contexts, 50% in 155 MB Glut, and no on-target FDR support. power_assessment: Reported positive programs are assessed across dominant and lower-yield contexts; 151/155 concentration is not penalized, lower-yield nulls are not specificity evidence, and self-RNA FDR is not an engagement gate.
adjudication_reason: The “Dhx9 and nuclear-pore transport perturbations expose a nuclear RNP/splicing state rather than Dicer/Ago or generic karyopherin loss” relationship is plausible, but unresolved causal or functional alternatives limit confidence and program scale.

title: Ahdc1 loss selectively depresses neuronal surface and synaptic transcripts in 151 TH without canonical Wnt activation
exact_observed_result: Ahdc1 perturbation produced an FDR-supported response only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, dominated by decreases in Ptprz1, Spock3, Lrp1b, Tro, Gria2, Cdh18, Ache, Calb1, and Wls without Axin2 or Nkd1 induction.
biological_interpretation: AHDC1 loss in the assayed thalamic neurons is better framed as neuronal surface/synaptic transcript loss than as an APC-like Wnt activation state.

title: Zbtb18 loss induces a thalamic Endou-Pxdn-Clstn2-Man2a2 program
exact_observed_result: Zbtb18 perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut induced Endou, Pxdn, Clstn2, Man2a2, and Zbtb18 at FDR<0.05, with Pxdn also FDR-supported in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut. Candidate co-repressors Dnmt3a and Ctbp1 did not reproduce the thalamic Endou/Pxdn/Clstn2/Man2a2 program.
biological_interpretation: The adult Zbtb18 response is a restricted thalamic and cortical glutamatergic output, not a generic readout of perturbing associated Dnmt3a/Ctbp1 co-repressors.

title: Core autophagy perturbations reduce ER-lumen and endomembrane transcripts in selected thalamic and midbrain neurons
exact_observed_result: Rb1cc1 loss produced corrected ER/endomembrane responses in 151 TH, 155 MB and 191 MB P MY GABA neurons, including Calr, Hspa5, Pdia6, Psap, Atp1a3 and Atp1b1 decreases. Atg5 was weaker but had a focal 155 MB Glut signature with Calr and Rtn1 down, and Becn1 had its only multi-gene FDR program in 155 MB Glut with Calr, Ctsb, Dnm1, Psma5 and Syt11 down.

title: PMCA1 loss selectively induces a thalamic calcium-activity and neurosecretory program

title: Mecp2 perturbation alters a sparse excitability and membrane-gene module rather than a universal Rett-like transcriptome
exact_observed_result: Mecp2 mRNA itself was not FDR-depleted in any measured class, but four of 22 cell types had FDR-supported downstream rows. The richest 151 TH Prkcd/Grin2c signature included Ache, Fxyd7, L1cam, Cacna1g, Mast1, and Mgat5 down plus Itpr1 and Kcnh5 up; Cacna1g was also FDR-down in 155 MB Glut, and Auts2 was the isolated Pvalb FDR hit.
biological_interpretation: Acute Mecp2 perturbation exposes a sparse cell-type-resolved excitability and membrane module, with Cacna1g and Auts2 as the cleanest markers, rather than a uniform Rett-like expression collapse or a single downstream rescue node.

title: TrkB loss represses Vgf-centered MAPK output in Pvalb and thalamic glutamatergic neurons
exact_observed_result: Ntrk2 was reduced in 22/22 assayed Ntrk2 cell types and reached FDR in Pvalb GABA, thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic cells, and 155 MB Glut. title: Partial loss of spliceosome and TREX factors drives posterior RNA-processing stress programs
exact_observed_result: Cdc40, Rnpc3, Thoc1 and Thoc2 each produced cell-gated RNA-processing responses: Cdc40 lowered Srrm2, Rsrp1, Srsf6 and Pabpn1 while increasing Pde4a in posterior neurons; Rnpc3 induced Pcyt2/Mapk8/Ap2a1/Rab6b/Smyd2/Srp72/Trit1 with Amy1/Tcea2 down in 151 TH; Thoc1 repressed Snhg11/Rsrp1/Fam193b and induced Smarcc2/Anxa6/Dgkz/Gtf2i in subcortical classes; Thoc2 was FDR-resolved only in 052 Pvalb. Snrnp70, Ascc3, Tardbp and Srrm2 supplied weaker convergence/non-interchangeability evidence tying these states to spliceosome, RNA-export and proteasome neighbors.
biological_interpretation: Posterior and selected inhibitory neurons are selectively sensitive to partial spliceosome/TREX disruption and shift into RNA-processing abundance states rather than showing uniform housekeeping collapse.

title: Lonp1 loss induces a Ddit3-centered mitochondrial ISR-like amino-acid module
exact_observed_result: Lonp1 perturbation induced Ddit3 in 217 P MY Pineal Glut and 155 MB Glut and Slc7a1 in 217 P MY Pineal Glut. title: HSPA5 perturbation activates a BiP-centered ER stress state that selectively converges with HSPA9 and UFMylation

title: Kdm5c, Nsd1, and Zmynd8 converge on a 151 TH chromatin-response hotspot with distinct repression outputs
exact_observed_result: Kdm5c, Nsd1, and Zmynd8 each produced FDR-supported 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut responses with an overlapping chromatin-linked hotspot including Ptgds, Capn3, Ache, Zfp532, Hexim2, Gabbr2, Nrxn1, Grm1, and Lrrc7, while Zmynd8 remained directionally distinct from related NuRD or ZMYND perturbations.
biological_interpretation: The result points to a thalamic chromatin-response hotspot shared by multiple disease-relevant regulators rather than a generic collapse shared by every chromatin perturbation.

title: BRD4 loss remodels synaptic and membrane transcripts in thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c neurons
exact_observed_result: Brd4 perturbation produced its largest corrected signature in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons, where Omg, Plch2, Sparcl1, Gria4, Gabrg2, Dpp6 and Mapk10 were reduced and Gabbr1, Gabbr2, Snap25 and Vamp2 were induced at FDR < 0.05. Yy1 perturbation aligned with Brd4, Chd8 and Trrap signatures more than with the flat Jarid2 PRC2-cofactor comparison.
biological_interpretation: The result supports a selective BET/chromatin-cofactor liability in thalamic glutamatergic neurons and connects BRD4 output to an active enhancer/cofactor neighborhood rather than to a generic chromatin-remodeler state.

title: Late endolysosomal and mTOR-regulatory losses induce a lysosomal-sterol module in TH and MB glutamatergic neurons
exact_observed_result: Vps41, Slc17a5, Rab7, Tsc1, and Tsc2 perturbations up-regulated lysosomal genes such as Mcoln1, Atp6v0b, Atp6v1b2, Lamp2, Gba, Dpp7, Gm2a and sterol genes including Insig1, Srebf2, Dhcr24, Msmo1, Fdps, and Cyp51 in selected TH/MB/P-MY neurons, while Ctsb remained buffered. / Slc17a5 perturbation produced FDR-resolved responses only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, while most tested cell types were buffered or underpowered despite nominal Slc17a5 lowering. / Slc17a5 restricted-signature neighbors preferentially implicated Vps41, Rab7, Tsc1/Tsc2, and V-ATPase perturbations, while Vps41 was closest to Rab7 and Tsc1/Tsc2-Dctn1/Dync1h1/Slc17a5 neighbors and only weakly related to retromer and GARP VPS-family perturbations. Parquet-verified leading rows: Ctsb->Ctsb in 155 MB Glut log2FC -2.41, FDR 3.08e-81; Ctsb->Ctsb in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut log2FC -1.48, FDR 8.54e-43; Ctsb->Ctsb in 191 MB P MY GABA log2FC -2.2, FDR 6.06e-31; Tsc1->Cpeb1 in 155 MB Glut log2FC 1.16, FDR 2.44e-28; Tsc1->Stmn4 in 155 MB Glut log2FC 1.29, FDR 2.90e-28; Tsc1->Atp6v0b in 155 MB Glut log2FC 0.526, FDR 1.40e-21.
biological_interpretation: Core late-endosome trafficking and TSC loss converge on a neuronal lysosomal-sterol stress state that is not triggered by loss of a terminal lysosomal protease. / Sialin loss generates a cell-state-restricted neuronal stress pattern and should not be treated as a broad neuronal transcriptome defect in this assay. / Sialin/SLC17A5 loss may impinge on a Rab7-HOPS lysosomal branch tied to mTOR/TFEB signaling, rather than generating a uniform lysosomal-storage or all-VPS trafficking RNA state.

title: PROX1 perturbation creates a thalamic transcription-factor state uncoupled from lymphatic VEGFC/FLT4/SOX18 circuitry
exact_observed_result: Prox1 guides produced a statistically resolved 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut response in which the measured Prox1 transcript increased and Tmem145/Vgf rose while Rreb1, Nexn, Snx25, and Kcnd2 fell; Flt4, Nr2f2, Sox18, and lymphatic VEGFC/PROX1 neighbors were inert in the same class.

title: Gabrg2 loss induces a weak glutamatergic Bdnf-Vgf activity response
exact_observed_result: Gabrg2 mRNA was strongly depleted in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, where Bdnf, Vgf, Nptx2, and Fosl2 trended upward; the Bdnf/Vgf arm was nominal-to-near-FDR rather than conventionally FDR-supported in the exact rows. Kcnb1 in the same cell type robustly induced Bdnf, Vgf, and Nptx2, while Gphn produced a narrow Cbarp signal.
biological_interpretation: The Gabrg2 result is consistent with reduced GABA-A gamma-2 inhibitory signaling inducing activity/trophic genes in selected glutamatergic cells, but the shared Gphn/Kcnb1 neighborhood is weak and should be kept as a restricted excitability-signature hint.
